proposals.name: Restore (and overshoot) the idiosyncratic cash-flow band, and hand the econometrician idiosyncratic volatility
proposals.one_line: Change the single hand-inserted 0.1 on panel_functions_bgn.py:54 to 1.75 and add a 60-month realized-volatility characteristic; this converts the true MVE weight into an explicit b(x)/d(x) ratio and opens a 21-percentage-point nonlinearity gap where there are currently 3.
proposals.economic_story: BGN's projects have idiosyncratic cash-flow risk on top of their systematic exposure. The code caps that idiosyncratic band at 0.1*0.3*|Cbar| = 0.111 in log-cash-flow units (line 54, comment '# added a factor of 0.1'), against a lower bound |beta|/sigma_z that averages ~1.6. The result is that project cash flows are 93% systematic (mean corr_zj = 0.958), average pairwise stock-return correlation is 0.48, and the cross-sectional dispersion of idiosyncratic variance is sd(log d) = 0.23 with max/min of 2.8. Real US equities have average pairwise correlation ~0.17-0.20, idiosyncratic share of variance ~0.70, monthly stock volatility ~12-13%, and sd(log idiosyncratic variance) ~1.0-1.3 with a range of two orders of magnitude. The model has essentially deleted firm-specific risk. Restoring it is a return toward BGN's own un-multiplied 0.3*|Cbar| band, not an invention. Economically: heterogeneous projects differ not only in how much aggregate risk they carry but in how much project-specific risk they carry. It does not touch BGN's identity: risk-neutral project value is Chat*exp(-beta_j) regardless of sigma_j, so prices, the investment threshold, the option value J*, and the ENTIRE expected-return vector are numerically UNCHANGED. Size and B/M remain sufficient statistics for expected returns; they cease to be sufficient for the covariance matrix, hence for the optimal portfolio.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Verified numerically (scratchpad/bgn_span3.py, N=250, exact rp and cond_var from sdf_compute_bgn.sdf_loop, correct span projector max_a SR(Xa) = |P_{col(L'X)} L^{-1} rp| with Sigma = LL'). BASELINE (band factor 0.1): mean vol 6.48%/mo, pairwise corr 0.479, sd(log d) 0.234, d_max/d_min 2.8, idio share 0.51, max_sr 0.2625. Span attained: {1, log mve, bm} 95.03%; {1, log mve, bm, log ivol} 95.85%; full quadratic in those 4 chars 99.32%; cubic in (log mve, bm) 98.72%; explicit 1/d ratio basis 96.27%. Total nonlinearity headroom: 3.5 points. AT BAND FACTOR 1.75: mean vol 12.30%/mo, pairwise corr 0.220, sd(log d) 1.212, d_max/d_min 4715, idio share 0.752, max_sr 0.2227. Span attained: {1, log mve, bm} 69.06%; adding log ivol LINEARLY 72.04%; full quadratic in the same 4 chars 93.53%; cubic in (log mve, bm) alone 82.32%; explicit 1/d ratio basis 98.14%. The population ceiling on DKKM-over-FM goes from 99.32/95.85 = 1.036x to 93.53/72.04 = 1.30x, and 1.36x if the basis reaches the exact reciprocal. Mechanism is exactly H2: w* = D^{-1}(rp - Bc); once d_i spans 3.7 orders of magnitude the 1/d factor dominates the cross-sectional variation of w*. The ivol characteristic makes 1/d learnable; the reciprocal keeps it out of the linear span.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's weights are w_i = a'x_i with one coefficient vector re-estimated monthly, so the FM weight span is exactly the linear span of the characteristic columns. The true MVE weight is w*_i = (rp_i - b_i'c)/d_i. Even though rp_i is linear in x (it is exactly affine in (1/mve, bm) - see Proposal 2) and log d_i is essentially linear in log ivol by construction, the RATIO is not: it is linear times exp(-linear), a function of unbounded curvature that no linear combination of the columns reproduces. The measured numbers are the proof: handing FM the log-volatility char raises it only 69.1% -> 72.0%, while the same four chars in a quadratic basis reach 93.5%. FF is worse for two reasons: (i) its factors are value-weighted 2x3 sorts, so each is a coarse 6-cell step function, and with d_i varying by 4700x a tercile bucket averages firms whose optimal weights differ by three orders of magnitude; (ii) value-weighting is close to the wrong tilt, since d_i falls with project count so the optimal weight rises with size in a strongly convex way that value-weighting mimics only linearly. DKKM's basis contains sin/cos of random linear indices in the rank-standardized chars including ivol, whose span covers 87-94% of the quadratic/cubic polynomial in those chars - precisely the 93.5% number.
proposals.exact_change: (1) utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py line 54: change `high=np.abs(beta[:-1, :]) / sigma_z + 0.1*0.3 * np.abs(Cbar),` to use a config constant BGN_SIGMAJ_BAND = 0.525 (= 1.75*0.3) added to config.py near CBAR (line 206) and imported at panel_functions_bgn.py lines 11-15. Delete the stale '# added a factor of 0.1' comment. NOTHING else in panel_functions_bgn.py changes: sigma_j does not enter the investment rule (line 82), beta_avg (lines 148-149), A (line 153), G (line 157), P (lines 161-164) or any of the four eret terms (lines 172-186). (2) utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py needs NO change: sigmaj enters only through col2/col3 (lines 163-164), exp_corr_zr (line 149) and the term4 diagonal corrections (lines 234-256), all already general in sigmaj. I ran the existing sdf_loop unmodified at band 1.75 and it returns a well-conditioned ER (no LinAlgWarning; the warning appears only at band >= 3). (3) New characteristic: in create_panel, after line 253 (the `mom` block) add `df['ivol'] = df.groupby('firmid', group_keys=False).ret.apply(lambda x: x.rolling(60, min_periods=24).std().shift(1))`, computed from `ret` BEFORE the risk-free subtraction at line 267 and shifted so it is date-t information. (4) config.py: add `CHARS_BGN = CHARS_DEFAULT + ['ivol']` and `FACTOR_NAMES_BGN = FACTOR_NAMES_DEFAULT + ['ivol']` after line 220; add `'ivol': 'ivol'` to CHAR_TO_FACTOR (line 229); set MODEL_CHARS['bgn'] = CHARS_BGN (line 318) and MODEL_FACTOR_NAMES['bgn'] = FACTOR_NAMES_BGN (line 325). Do NOT edit CHARS_DEFAULT itself - kp14 shares it.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: The band multiplier is the only new number. I scanned it with the actual code (multiplier m replaces the 0.1, so band width = m*0.3*|Cbar| = 1.11*m): m=0.1 (current) -> vol 6.5%/mo, pairwise corr 0.479, sd(log d) 0.234, idio share 0.510; m=1.0 (BGN's un-multiplied band) -> 6.9%, 0.421, 0.309, 0.567; m=1.25 -> 7.6%, 0.369, 0.633, 0.618; m=1.5 -> 9.0%, 0.297, 0.872, 0.681; m=1.75 -> 12.3%, 0.220, 1.212, 0.752; m=2.0 -> 19.9%, 0.152, 1.471, 0.989; m=2.5 -> 81.8%, 0.069, 2.743, 0.991. Targets: monthly individual-stock volatility 12-13% (CRSP median), average pairwise correlation 0.17-0.20, idiosyncratic share 0.65-0.75, and sd(log idiosyncratic variance) 1.0-1.3 (the moment the BGN diagnosis flagged as 0.263 vs 1.0-1.3 in real data). m=1.75 hits ALL FOUR simultaneously (12.3%, 0.220, 0.752, 1.212). m=2.0 overshoots volatility by 60% and the lognormal blows up beyond that. So m = 1.75, i.e. replace `0.1*0.3` with `0.525`. Cost check: max_sr falls 0.2625 -> 0.2227/month (annualized 0.91 -> 0.77), moving the model toward, not away from, plausible values.
proposals.predicted_effect: max_sr: 0.2625 -> 0.2227/month (a 15% fall; desirable, the model was too easy). FF/FM Sharpe: falls hard, from ~0.95*max to ~0.72*max, i.e. realized FM from 0.2357 to roughly 0.15-0.16; FF falls further because step-function weights cannot track 1/d, expect 0.10-0.13. DKKM: with the CURRENT RFF basis (87-94% inside the cubic span) expect 0.82-0.93 of max, i.e. 0.18-0.21; with Proposal 3's bandwidth rescale, ~0.21. Predicted realized DKKM/FF ratio 1.4-1.8x versus 1.04x today. HJD population floors, sqrt(S*^2/(1+S*^2) - S_f^2/(1+S_f^2)) at S* = 0.2227: FM 0.149, DKKM-quadratic 0.075, DKKM-with-reciprocal 0.041, no-position 0.218. The same computation at baseline (S* = 0.2625) gives FM 0.070 and DKKM 0.029, so absolute HJD rises for everyone but the FM-minus-DKKM difference goes from 0.041 to 0.074. Honest caveat: the published HJDs (FF 0.218, FM 0.223, DKKM 0.201) sit far above these floors, so realized HJD is estimation-noise dominated; the Sharpe prediction is the reliable one.
risks: At m=1.75, sigma_j reaches ~2.7 in log-cash-flow units, so project cash flows are extremely right-skewed lognormals. Realized roe and payout become heavy-tailed and a referee may object that a 270% monthly log-sd is not a cash flow. Equivalent-moment reformulation: keep BGN's 0.3*|Cbar| band but multiply the idiosyncratic component by a lognormal project-level scale, sigma_j^2 = beta_j^2/sigma_z^2 + omega_j with log omega_j Gaussian, calibrated to the same sd(log d) = 1.2.

The gain is a CEILING, not a realization. DKKM must estimate the 1/d tilt from 360 months, and the RFF basis lies 93.6% inside the cubic span with every feature rank-standardized into [-0.5, 0.5] - exactly the wrong shape for a function that must be large on a few low-d firms. Ship with Proposal 3.

Conditioning: d_max/d_min goes 2.8 -> 4715. sdf_loop still solves cleanly at m=1.75 (verified, no LinAlgWarning) but at m=3.0 scipy reports rcond ~ 1e-24. Do not exceed 2.0, and add an eigenvalue-floor check at sdf_compute_bgn.py lines 306-317.

Higher idiosyncratic volatility mechanically adds noise to roe, agr and mom, hurting all methods' estimation and possibly DKKM's high-dimensional fit most. The population span numbers do not capture this.
proposals.implementation_cost: Essentially free. sdf_compute_bgn.sdf_loop is unchanged - I ran it at m=1.75 and it produced the reported moments at the same speed, because sigma_j already enters only through data-level multiplies on already-built sparse matrices (col2 line 163, col3 line 164, exp_corr_zr line 149, diag4 lines 234-256). The O(N^2) kron cost per month is identical. The conditional second moment stays exactly analytic: the lognormal cross-moment E[C_i C_j] = Chat^2 exp(sigma_i sigma_j corr_i corr_j) holds for any sigma_j. No solution file is re-solved - Jstar.csv, integrand_optval and integrand_optval_sq (sdf_compute_bgn.py lines 49-84) depend only on the beta distribution and on D(r), neither of which moves.

proposals.name: Break the exact rp = a + b/mve + (Chat*pi)*bm identity with a project-scale / intangible-capital wedge
proposals.one_line: Give each project an independent mean-one economic scale kappa_j that scales its cost and its cash flow but NOT its reported book value, so expected returns depend on a third firm state (economic capital) observable only through noisy payout yields.
proposals.economic_story: I verified algebraically and numerically (scratchpad/bgn_affine.py: R^2 = 1.0000, max |residual| = 3e-16 at three separate months) that in BGN as implemented the true conditional expected excess return is EXACTLY affine in two characteristics: eret_i,t = a_t + b_t*(1/mve_i) + (Chat*pi)*bm_i, with the bm coefficient equal to Chat*pi = 0.0244763 identically at every date. It follows mechanically: eret's term4 (line 181) is Chat*pi*book, term2 (line 176) is pi*A*E[D]/D with A = P - G, and terms 1 and 3 are date-level scalars, so 1 + eret_i = (c1+c3)/P_i + pi*e_t*(P_i - G_t)/P_i + Chat*pi*book_i/P_i. Two characteristics span the entire cross-section of expected returns exactly. That is the deepest reason nothing can beat FM here. The single assumption producing it is that expected cash flow per unit of BOOK capital is the same constant Chat for every project. Relax exactly that: project j has economic scale kappa_j (mean 1), so its investment cost is I*kappa_j and its cash flow is I*kappa_j*C_j, while reported book still records I per project. Because cost and payoff scale together the exercise rule exp(Cbar - beta_j)*D(r) > 1 is unchanged, J* is unchanged (E[kappa] = 1), and the beta calibration (prob_in_money 10% at r=0, 5% at rbar) is untouched. What changes is that book equity ceases to measure economic capital - the central measurement fact of the modern value literature (expensed intangible investment; Peters-Taylor, Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou). BGN's identity survives in its correct form: a firm is still a portfolio of heterogeneous projects valued at the sum of risk-neutral project values, but B/M becomes a NOISY proxy for the value-to-capital ratio rather than a sufficient statistic.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With kappa, eret's term4 becomes pi*Chat*I*Lambda_i where Lambda_i = sum_j chi_j*kappa_j is economic capital, so eret_i = a_t + b_t/mve_i + pi*Chat*I*(Lambda_i/mve_i). Lambda_i/mve_i is a THIRD state, orthogonal by construction to bm_i = I*num_i/mve_i (their ratio Lambda_i/num_i is an independent mean-one average of num_i draws). It is unobservable. What IS observable is the realized payout yield y_it = I*sum_j kappa_j*C_j/mve_i, an unbiased but very noisy signal of Chat*Lambda_i/mve_i: per-project noise-to-signal is sqrt(exp(sigma_j^2)-1), currently ~3.8, attenuated by 1/sqrt(num_i) and by the averaging horizon. So E[Lambda_i/mve_i | data] = pi_i*y_bar_i + (1-pi_i)*prior with a FIRM-SPECIFIC shrinkage pi_i = s^2/(s^2 + noise_i^2/(num_i*H)) depending on the firm's cash-flow volatility, project count and horizon. The optimal predictor is a PRODUCT of a nonlinear function of (num_i, ivol_i) with the observed payout yield - a genuine three-way interaction, and exactly the mechanism by which complexity pays in real data (noisy redundant proxies for a latent state combined with signal-dependent shrinkage). It also raises cross-sectional predictive R^2 from 0.043%/month, an order of magnitude BELOW real data, to ~0.5%.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's monthly cross-sectional projection X(X'X)^{-1} applies ONE coefficient to the payout-yield column for every firm. The efficient weight pi_i varies across firms by an order of magnitude because noise_i^2/num_i does. FM can implement only the average shrinkage; the loss is the cross-sectional variance of (pi_i - pi_bar)*y_i, which is first-order because the noise in y_i dominates. Formally, the target g(num_i, ivol_i)*y_i lies in the linear span of the characteristics only if g is constant. FF is more restricted still: its 2x3 double sorts give weights piecewise constant on a 6-cell partition of (size, one other char), which can represent a two-level size-by-payout interaction but cannot represent the ivol dimension of the shrinkage at all (FF never sorts one non-size char against another) and cannot represent attenuation within a tercile. DKKM's RFF over (size, bm, payout, payout12, num, ivol) contains, to ~87% of its variance, the full quadratic in those chars, hence every pairwise product g_k(x)*y and a second-order-accurate shrinkage rule.
proposals.exact_change: (1) utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py after line 46: `kappa = np.exp(SIGMA_KAPPA*norm.rvs(size=(T, N)) - 0.5*SIGMA_KAPPA**2)`. (2) line 128: `op_cash_flow[t,:] = I*(kappa[:t+1,:]*C[t,:t+1,:]*chi[t+1,:t+1,:]).sum(axis=0)`. (3) line 133: `free_cash_flow = -I*kappa*np.float64(invest)`. (4) lines 148-153: replace `a = (chi*np.exp(-beta)).sum(axis=1)` / beta_avg / `A = book*Chat*beta_avg*bond_values` with `a = (chi*kappa*np.exp(-beta)).sum(axis=1)` and `A = I*Chat*a*bond_values`. Line 144 (`book = I*num`) is UNCHANGED - that is the whole point. (5) line 181: `term4 = Chat*pi*I*(chi*kappa).sum(axis=1)` in place of `Chat*pi*book`. (6) Return kappa in the arr_tuple (line 193) and unpack in create_panel (line 198) and sdf_compute (line 131). (7) utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py: put kappa on the valuation legs - line 162 `col1 = chisp.multiply(exp_beta[:t+1,:]*kappa[:t+1,:])`, line 164 `col3 = chisp.multiply(exp_corr_zr[:t+1,:]*kappa[:t+1,:])`. col2 (line 163) must NOT get kappa because it is exponentiated; instead build `colK = chisp.multiply(kappa[:t+1,:])` and change line 185 to `result4.data = np.exp(result4.data) * kron(colK, colK).data` (identical sparsity patterns, so a data-level multiply). (8) Diagonal corrections: lines 220-231 (diag3_sub) and 234-256 (diag4_sub, diag4_add) multiply the summand by kappa^2; lines 259-265 (diag5_sub) already inherits kappa twice via col1 and col3, so remove one factor. (9) lines 214-218 (term2t, option-times-option): multiply the i=j correction by E[kappa^2] = exp(SIGMA_KAPPA^2), since the new project's scale is drawn independently at t+1. (10) New chars in create_panel: `payout = op_cash_flow/mve` plus 12- and 60-month trailing means, and `nproj = book/I` (must be computed before the drop at line 264); register them in CHARS_BGN as in Proposal 1. (11) config.py: add SIGMA_KAPPA near line 206.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: One new parameter, SIGMA_KAPPA = sd(log kappa). Anchor 1 (cross-sectional predictability): the new premium term is pi*Chat*I*Lambda_i/mve_i; with num ~ 6 live projects and mve ~ 8, sd(Lambda) = sqrt(num*(exp(s^2)-1))*exp(s^2/2), so added dispersion of expected returns = 0.0245*sd(Lambda)/8. At s = 0.5: sd(Lambda) = sqrt(6*0.284)*1.133 = 1.48, giving 0.45%/month against a current TOTAL sd(rp) of 0.137%/month; with baseline volatility 6.5%/month that is a monthly cross-sectional R^2 of (0.0045/0.065)^2 = 0.48% versus real data's ~0.5%. So SIGMA_KAPPA = 0.5 standalone. Anchor 2 (combined with Proposal 1, volatility 12.3%/month): keeping R^2 at 0.5% needs sd(rp) = 0.87%/month, hence sd(Lambda) = 2.84 and s = 0.75. Anchor 3 (direct economic cross-check): sd(log(Lambda_i/num_i)) = sqrt((exp(s^2)-1)/num) = 0.22 at s=0.5 and 0.34 at s=0.75, i.e. a 10th-90th spread in the economic-to-book capital ratio of 1.8x and 2.4x; Peters-Taylor's intangible share of total capital runs from ~0.1 to ~0.7, a total/tangible spread of ~3x, so s = 0.75 is conservative. RECOMMENDATION: SIGMA_KAPPA = 0.75 with Proposal 1, 0.5 alone.
proposals.predicted_effect: max_sr: rises, since a new largely un-hedgeable premium dimension is added while the covariance is nearly unchanged; expect 0.26 -> 0.35-0.45/month standalone. Cross-sectional R^2 of returns on chars: 0.043% -> ~0.5%. FF/FM Sharpe: the linear span still captures the (1/mve, bm) part exactly and the payout signal with a single average shrinkage, so FM should attain ~70-80% of max rather than 95%; FF loses more because the signal needs a firm-specific weight and FF offers 6 cells. DKKM: 88-95% of max, giving DKKM/FM ~1.2-1.35x from this channel alone and ~1.6-2.0x stacked with Proposal 1. HJD floors: at S* = 0.40 with FM at 0.75*S* and DKKM at 0.92*S*, floors are 0.196 and 0.104, a 1.9x gap versus 1.04x today. Honest caveat: I did not simulate this one; Proposal 1's span numbers are measured, these are derived from the verified affine identity plus the measured baseline.
risks: The kappa weighting must go in exactly the right places in sdf_compute_bgn.py: valuation legs (col1, col3) take kappa once each; the exponentiated leg (col2) must not; term4's summand takes kappa twice OUTSIDE the exp; three diagonal corrections plus term2t need kappa^2 or E[kappa^2]. One mistake silently biases cond_var - the exact bug class already documented for kp14. Validate by Monte Carlo: simulate R_{t+1} many times at a fixed t and check the simulated second moment matches sdf_loop's ER elementwise.

A referee can object that if kappa scales cost and payoff identically a rational accountant would capitalize it. The answer is the intangible-investment literature (expensed R&D, organization capital), where economic and reported capital diverge one-for-one. Frame it that way, not as 'project scale'.
If SIGMA_KAPPA is too large, project count stops being informative and bm degenerates toward noise, harming all methods and possibly flattening the gap. Keep sd(log(Lambda/num)) below ~0.4.

The channel needs the payout signal noisy enough to require shrinkage but informative enough to use. At Proposal 1's band the noise may be so large that optimal shrinkage is near zero and the channel dies. Check the implied R^2 of E[Lambda/mve] on the payout chars first; if below ~0.1, lengthen the averaging-horizon chars (60m, 120m) rather than lowering the band.
proposals.implementation_cost: Small. The conditional second moment stays fully analytic: kappa_j is known at t, so every cross-moment picks up a deterministic kappa_j*kappa_k factor that multiplies (never enters) the existing lognormal exponentials. Runtime cost is one extra kron per month on term4 with a sparsity pattern identical to the existing one, so a data-level multiply - well under 10% added to sdf_loop's O(N^2 * nnz) cost. No solution file is re-solved: J*, integrand_optval and integrand_optval_sq depend only on the distribution of Cbar - beta and on D(r), and kappa cancels out of the exercise rule because it scales cost and payoff identically. Note BGN's moments step already runs at n_jobs = 1 (config.py line 40) so any added cost is serial.

proposals.name: Fix the characteristic set: repair agr, add the observables the model already generates, and rescale the RFF bandwidth for the new L
proposals.one_line: Replace the 91%-tied agr with 12-month book growth, add age / project count / payout yields at three horizons / idiosyncratic volatility / lagged bm / multi-horizon past returns, and multiply GAMMA_GRID by sqrt(130/L); the precondition without which none of the other proposals is visible to DKKM.
proposals.economic_story: The econometrician is given five characteristics, one of which (agr) is 91% ties at exactly zero because book = I*num is a small integer that changes only on a project birth or death. rank_standardize breaks those ties with np.argsort (dkkm_functions.py line 57), producing a persistent (0.92 autocorrelation) pseudo-random column that enters every one of DKKM's 3600 features MULTIPLICATIVELY while polluting only one of FM's six regressors additively. The same degeneracy makes FF's cma sort a 92/0/8 split with empty medium portfolios (agr q30 = q70 = 0). So one sixth of the information set is noise, asymmetrically worse for DKKM. Meanwhile the model generates - and a real econometrician would observe - at least six more things never handed over: firm age, live project count, payout yield and its trailing averages, realized volatility, investment frequency, and past returns at horizons other than 2-12. In real data DKKM's advantage with only five characteristics is 2.6-3.4x, so this is not about the count; it is about supplying the variables through which the latent states are imperfectly revealed. Finally sd(Wx) = gamma*sqrt(L/12) = 0.48 at L = 5, putting sin() on its linear arch: 78.8% of sin features are exactly monotone across the cross-section and the whole 3600-feature basis lies 93.6% inside the 56-dimensional cubic span. The bandwidth must scale with L.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: This creates no new economics; it removes three mechanical throttles. (a) agr: replacing pct_change on a small integer with 12-month growth book_t/book_{t-12} - 1 takes the number of distinct values from ~13 to ~40 and the tie mass from 91% to under 20%, which per the diagnosis reduces the feature principal components needed for 99% of variance from 95 back toward the 59 obtained with agr removed entirely - it stops spending a third of the effective feature rank on a pseudo-random column. (b) Characteristics: 1/d and the shrinkage weights of Proposals 1 and 2 are functions of ivol, num and payout; without those columns in MODEL_CHARS the nonlinear targets are not measurable functions of the inputs and DKKM's ceiling equals FM's. (c) Bandwidth: with L = 11 chars, sqrt(130/11) = 3.44, so GAMMA_GRID becomes [1.72, 2.06, 2.41, 2.75, 3.10, 3.44]. The measured effect of a comparable rescale is participation-ratio effective rank 14-16 -> ~78, linear-span share 49% -> 14%, cubic-span share 88% -> 52% - which is what lets the basis represent a reciprocal rather than a cubic, i.e. the difference between the 93.5% and 98.1% numbers measured in Proposal 1.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: Partially it CAN, and this must be stated honestly. Adding characteristics enlarges FM's linear span too, and FM will gain from a clean agr and a payout column. The asymmetries are three and specific: (i) the agr tie-breaking damages DKKM multiplicatively (every feature) and FM additively (one regressor), so repairing it is an asymmetric DKKM gain; (ii) FF's cma sort is currently a degenerate 92/0/8 split with literally empty middle portfolios, so repairing agr repairs one of FF's seven factors, but FF still cannot use ivol or num except through a size double-sort; (iii) the bandwidth rescale is a DKKM-only knob with no FF/FM counterpart. Honest summary: on its own this moves the DKKM/FM ratio by perhaps 1.02-1.05x. Its value is as a multiplier on Proposals 1, 2, 4 and 5, whose targets are functions of the new columns and whose curvature exceeds what a gamma = 0.5-1.0 basis can express.
proposals.exact_change: (1) utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py lines 255-260: replace the one-month `x.pct_change()` agr with `x/x.shift(12) - 1` (guarding x.shift(12) > 0). (2) After line 253 add `df['age'] = df.groupby('firmid').cumcount()`; `df['nproj'] = df.book / I`; `df['payout'] = df.op_cash_flow/df.mve` plus 12- and 60-month trailing means; `df['ivol']` as the 60-month rolling sd of ret, shifted one month; `df['bm_lag'] = df.groupby('firmid').bm.shift(12)`; `df['ret1'] = df.groupby('firmid').ret.shift(1)`; `df['ret13_60'] = cumret.shift(13)/cumret.shift(61) - 1`. Line 264 currently drops book, cumret and op_cash_flow - keep the derived columns. (3) config.py after line 220: `CHARS_BGN = ['size','bm','agr','roe','mom','age','nproj','payout','payout12','ivol','ret13_60']`, a matching FACTOR_NAMES_BGN, entries in CHAR_TO_FACTOR (line 229), and MODEL_CHARS['bgn'] / MODEL_FACTOR_NAMES['bgn'] at lines 318 and 325. (4) config.py line 211: make the bandwidth L-aware, `GAMMA_GRID_BGN = np.arange(0.5, 1.1, 0.1)*np.sqrt(130/len(CHARS_BGN))`, threaded through utils/generate_dkkm_factors.py line 115 where gamma_i is drawn. (5) Recommended alongside: config.py line 178 NMAT = 5 -> 1 (the root codebase used 1; averaging 5 independent W draws converges to kernel ridge and cancels exactly the draw-specific high-frequency directions complexity is supposed to exploit), and replace ALPHA_LST (line 190) with a grid that visits the mildly-overparameterized region - the current grid jumps from effective df 360 at alpha=0 to df 63 at alpha=0.001, skipping the entire df in (63, 360) band where the virtue of complexity peaks; use [0, 3e-5, 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2, 3e-2, 1e-1, 1].
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: The bandwidth multiplier is derived, not tuned: the pre-activation index is z = gamma*w'x with w ~ N(0, I_L) and each rank-standardized char having variance 1/12, so sd(z) = gamma*sqrt(L/12). Didisheim-Ke-Kelly-Malamud use the same gamma grid [0.5,...,1.0] with L = 130, giving sd(z) = 3.29*gamma; to reproduce that effective bandwidth at L chars multiply gamma by sqrt(130/L), which is 3.44 at L = 11. Closed-form check: for u ~ N(0, s^2) the R^2 of the linear projection of sin(u) on u is 2 s^2 exp(-s^2)/(1 - exp(-2 s^2)) - 0.998 at s = 0.32 (current) and 0.02 at s = 1.6 (rescaled). The 60-month volatility window is the standard low-frequency idiosyncratic-volatility construction and, with burnin = 200 and evaluation starting at burnin + 360, full history is always available. The 12-month agr horizon matches the standard Cooper-Gulen-Schill asset-growth definition.
proposals.predicted_effect: Standalone: max_sr unchanged (nothing in the model's moments moves). FF Sharpe: small improvement, because cma stops being a degenerate 92/0/8 sort. FM Sharpe: small improvement from a cleaner agr and six more spanning directions, perhaps 0.236 -> 0.24-0.25. DKKM Sharpe: improvement from a cleaner feature space and a genuinely nonlinear basis, but on the CURRENT model the ceiling is 98.7% versus FM's 95.0%, so at most 0.253 -> 0.258. Net DKKM/FF ~1.05x - this proposal alone does NOT solve the problem. Its predicted effect in combination is large: it converts Proposal 1's measured 93.5%-versus-72.0% population ceiling into a realized gap, and without it Proposal 1's ivol char cannot be used nonlinearly and Proposal 2's shrinkage interaction cannot be formed at all.
risks: Adding characteristics helps FM mechanically. If the new premium dimensions are linear in the new chars, this shrinks rather than widens the gap. Only ship with a model change whose target is demonstrably nonlinear.

The bandwidth rescale is double-edged: an independent experiment found a x8 rescale HURT badly when the truth was low-order (0.157 vs 0.254) and helped only with genuine high-frequency content. Apply it after, not before, Proposals 1 and 2 - with a near-linear truth a narrow kernel is the right kernel.

The second rank-standardization at dkkm_functions.py line 110 makes gamma a near no-op for 76% of features (rank-standardizing a monotone transform returns the rank of the argument), so rescaling gamma alone recovers only the sin-folding part of the effect. Consider replacing that second rank_standardize with per-column unit-variance standardization - but note that simply DELETING it raises the linear share from 49% to 86%, so it must be replaced, not removed.
NMAT = 1 raises the Monte-Carlo variance of DKKM's weights fivefold; report the five draws as replications rather than averaging, or the comparison becomes noisier for DKKM only.
proposals.implementation_cost: Free on the moments side: nothing in sdf_compute_bgn.py changes, the O(N^2) per-month cost is untouched, and no analytic moment is affected because every new column is a deterministic function of already-simulated panel quantities. Costs are in the estimation step: raising L from 5 to 11 makes W an (1800, 12) matrix instead of (1800, 6) (utils/generate_dkkm_factors.py line 113-119), a trivial change, and adds five columns to the FF/FM factor sets so those steps grow linearly. The only real cost is re-running the whole pipeline.

proposals.name: Cohort (vintage) common cash-flow factors: unpriced comovement whose hedge weights are non-monotone in firm age
proposals.one_line: Let projects born in the same period share a common cash-flow shock with correlation decaying across vintages, so a firm's factor exposures are the value shares of its project age distribution - a set of bump functions of firm age that six linear characteristic portfolios cannot zero out.
proposals.economic_story: BGN's firms are portfolios of projects, but the projects are currently independent conditional on the single aggregate shock nu, which is what makes the conditional covariance a one-strong-factor-plus-diagonal object (top eigenvalue 56% of variance, second 66x smaller). In reality, projects adopted at the same time embed the same technological vintage and are hit by common obsolescence and relative-price shocks - the vintage-capital tradition (Solow, Greenwood-Hercowitz-Krusell) and, in asset pricing, the investment-specific technology channel of Papanikolaou and Kogan-Papanikolaou. A cohort factor is the most BGN-native way to raise the number of common shocks without touching the pricing kernel: because cohort shocks are orthogonal to nu they carry no price of risk, so the risk-neutral cash flow of every project remains Chat*exp(-beta_j), and prices, the exercise rule, J*, optval and the entire expected-return vector are UNCHANGED - BGN's sufficiency claim for expected returns is preserved literally. What changes is that the covariance matrix acquires K_eff additional common factors that must be HEDGED, with exposures equal to the firm's project-age composition.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: With Sigma = BB' + D and B now having 2 + K_eff columns, the optimum w* = D^{-1}B(I + B'D^{-1}B)^{-1}lambda must be exposed to the priced column and NEUTRAL to all K_eff cohort columns. Firm i's exposure to cohort m is phi_m(i) = the value share of its live projects born in window m, which given pi = 0.99 is in expectation a function of firm age: zero for cohorts older than the firm, rising over the next few decay lengths, then geometrically declining. Each phi_m is a BUMP in age. A portfolio whose weights are affine in age can zero at most one linear combination of these exposures; with K_eff cohort factors it carries K_eff - 1 uncontrolled. A basis containing bump functions of age can zero all of them. The BGN-specific amplification: the investment rule already selects on beta as a function of the interest rate at birth (line 82: invest iff exp(Cbar - beta)*D(r_s) > 1, so the beta cutoff is Cbar + log D(r_s)), which concentrates high-beta, high-premium projects in low-rate vintages. A premium-seeking portfolio is therefore FORCED to concentrate its cohort exposure rather than spread it - precisely the condition under which cohort risk does not diversify away.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: FM's weights are w = a'x with a re-estimated monthly, so the achievable cohort-exposure vectors {sum_i (a'x_i) phi_m(i)}_m form an L-dimensional subspace of the K_eff-dimensional exposure space. With L = 6 and K_eff = 20 the best achievable Sharpe is |P_V Theta| for that 6-dimensional V, at most sqrt(6/20) = 0.55 of the maximum for generic Theta, and strictly less than the maximum whenever K_eff > L. This is dimension counting, not approximation - airtight. FF is strictly worse: seven factors, weights piecewise constant on tercile cells, and it never sorts on age at all. DKKM's span of achievable weight vectors has dimension equal to the effective rank of its feature matrix (14-16 as configured, ~78 with Proposal 3's bandwidth), so it can zero K_eff exposures provided K_eff is below that rank and the phi_m are learnable functions of the supplied chars (age, nproj, agr history), which by construction they are.
proposals.exact_change: (1) utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py lines 69-76. Currently `cash_shocks = np.random.standard_normal((T-1,T-1,N))` and `eps = nu[t+1]*corr_zj + sqrt(1-corr_zj^2)*cash_shocks`. Insert a cohort layer: draw `w_coh = np.random.standard_normal((T-1, T-1))` (date t+1 by vintage s, COMMON across firms), smooth across vintages with `v_coh[t,:] = Lchol @ w_coh[t,:]` where Lchol = cholesky of K with K[s,s'] = RHO_COH**abs(s-s'), and set `eps = corr_zj*nu[t+1] + sqrt(1-corr_zj**2)*(A0_COH*v_coh[t,:,None] + sqrt(1-A0_COH**2)*cash_shocks[t])`. v_coh is indexed by the project's BIRTH date s, which is exactly the second axis of cash_shocks, so the broadcast is free. (2) utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py: the only affected object is E[C_i C_j] = Chat^2*exp(sigma_i sigma_j [corr_i corr_j + a0^2 sqrt(1-corr_i^2) sqrt(1-corr_j^2) rho^|s_i - s_j|]). Add `col2v = chisp.multiply(sigmaj[:t+1,:]*np.sqrt(1-corr_zj[:t+1,:]**2)*A0_COH)` next to col2 at line 163. At lines 184-186 build `resultV = kron(col2v, col2v)` (identical sparsity to result4) and set `result4.data = np.exp(result4.data + kern_row[resultV.tocoo().row]*resultV.data)`, where kern_row is the length-(t+1)^2 vector RHO_COH**|s - s'| built once per month from the kron row index (row = s*(t+1) + s'). (3) Diagonal corrections lines 234-256: diag4_sub must use exp(sigmaj^2*(corr_zj^2 + (1-corr_zj^2)*A0_COH^2)) instead of exp(sigmaj^2*corr_zj^2), since rho^0 = 1 for a project with itself. (4) Nothing else changes - terms 3, 5, 7, 8 involve corr_zr and the valuation legs, and the cohort shocks are orthogonal to xi and to log M. (5) config.py: add A0_COH and RHO_COH near line 206. (6) Add `age` to CHARS_BGN as in Proposal 3 - without it the exposures are unlearnable and every method scores zero.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: RHO_COH sets the number of effective cohort factors. With pi = 0.99 the expected project life is 100 months and the live-project age distribution has an effective width of ~250-300 months in a T = 720 panel. For an AR kernel with correlation length h = -1/log(RHO_COH), the number of eigenvalues of K above a tenth of the leading one over a window Wd is roughly Wd/(pi*h). Requiring K_eff comfortably above the L = 6-11 characteristic dimensions and comfortably below DKKM's effective feature rank (14-16 as configured, ~78 after the bandwidth rescale) gives K_eff in [15, 40], hence h in [2.5, 6] months for Wd = 300 - so RHO_COH = exp(-1/4) = 0.78 as a central choice, giving h = 4 months and K_eff ~ 24, with same-vintage correlation 0.05 at a 12-month separation (high within a year, negligible across a decade, which is the right qualitative shape for vintage productivity). A0_COH is the share of NON-systematic cash-flow variance that is cohort-common. Target the variance decomposition of individual stock returns - roughly 20-25% market, 8-12% industry/cohort-like common, 65-70% idiosyncratic. At Proposal 1's calibration the non-systematic cash-flow channel supplies ~75% of return variance, so A0_COH^2 = 0.10/0.75 = 0.133, i.e. A0_COH = 0.37. Without Proposal 1 the non-systematic channel is only 7% of cash-flow variance and A0_COH cannot buy anything - this proposal REQUIRES Proposal 1.
proposals.predicted_effect: max_sr: falls modestly (5-15%), since cohort variance is added with no premium. FF/FM Sharpe: falls by the dimension-counting factor. With K_eff = 24 and L = 11 chars, the pessimistic bound is sqrt(11/24) = 0.68 of max, but the realistic figure is higher because cohort exposures partially diversify (a diversified portfolio's cohort exposure falls as 1/sqrt(K_eff)), so the honest range is 0.75-0.90 of max for FM against 0.95+ for DKKM, i.e. DKKM/FM of 1.1-1.3x. HJD floors widen correspondingly. This is my least certain magnitude: an independent theory experiment found that under exact factor pricing with N = 1000 a well-diversified portfolio attains the maximum Sharpe to within 0.19%, and the only reason a cohort structure escapes that is that the premium-seeking tilt is forced to be cohort-concentrated by BGN's own interest-rate-dependent exercise rule. If that concentration is weak the gain is at the low end. It is testable before implementing: at a single month, regress the true MVE weight on the firm-age profile and check whether the FM-span-optimal portfolio's implied cohort exposure is materially nonzero.
risks: Diversification may kill it. A char portfolio's exposure to cohort m is a population average, so it is O(1) only if the weights are age-tilted; if not, cohort risk diversifies as 1/sqrt(K_eff) and the gain collapses to a few percent. Run the diagnostic above first.
It requires Proposal 1. With the current 0.1 band there is only 7% of non-systematic cash-flow variance to allocate to cohorts, so A0_COH is bounded and the factor is invisible.

Implementation risk in the kron: the cohort kernel enters as a per-ROW multiplier on kron(col2v, col2v), and getting the row-index-to-(s, s') mapping wrong (kron row = s*(t+1) + s' with the first operand outer) silently produces the wrong covariance with no error raised. Verify against a brute-force double loop at small N.

Runtime: term4 currently costs one kron of a (t+1) x N sparse matrix with itself; this adds a second. Since term4 is one of roughly six O(N^2 * nnz) terms, expect a 15-20% increase in sdf_loop time on top of BGN's already-serial moments step (config.py line 40, n_jobs = 1).
The eps construction at line 75 already dominates BGN's memory as a (T-1) x (T-1) x N object; build v_coh once and broadcast rather than materializing another array of that shape.
proposals.implementation_cost: Moderate but bounded, and the second moment stays exactly analytic. The lognormal cross-moment generalizes without any new quadrature: E[C_i C_j] = Chat^2 exp(sigma_i sigma_j [corr_i corr_j + a0^2 sqrt(1-corr_i^2)sqrt(1-corr_j^2) rho^|s_i-s_j|]), and because the vintage kernel depends only on the pair of BIRTH DATES it is a function of the kron ROW index alone, so it is a precomputed length-(t+1)^2 vector multiplied into the data before exponentiation. No new integral, no new interpolant. One extra sparse kron per month with a sparsity pattern identical to the existing term4, giving roughly a 15-20% increase in the O(N^2) per-month cost. No solution file is re-solved - the cohort shocks are orthogonal to log M, so Chat*exp(-beta_j), the exercise rule, Jstar.csv, integrand_optval and integrand_optval_sq are untouched.

proposals.name: HIGH RISK / HIGH REWARD: a characteristic-dependent clientele demand wedge (an AIPT alpha)
proposals.one_line: Multiply each firm's price by a slow-moving, mean-reverting demand wedge whose target is a deliberately non-monotone, interactive function of characteristics - the only change that gives BGN a premium component not proportional to any covariance loading, which theory says is the necessary condition for complexity to pay.
proposals.economic_story: Every other proposal leaves BGN a frictionless representative-agent economy with a one-dimensional price-of-risk vector, and in such an economy the maximum Sharpe is |Theta| and the appraisal ratio of any residual is exactly zero. The DKKM/AIPT theory is explicit that the virtue of complexity requires an expected-return component NOT spanned by the dominant covariance loadings, whose squared Sharpe contribution alpha'D^{-1}alpha grows with N. An oracle span experiment run for this project makes the point quantitatively: with exact factor pricing the RFF-over-linear ceiling ratio is 0.994; with a LINEAR alpha and homogeneous d it is 1.00; with a linear alpha and heteroskedastic d it is 1.91; with a NONLINEAR alpha and heteroskedastic d it is 21. So the honest position is that a 3-5x DKKM advantage is unreachable without this ingredient, and the respectable way to add it is a segmented-clientele / demand-system wedge (Koijen-Yogo, Gabaix-Koijen) rather than 'mispricing': a subset of marginal investors holds characteristic-tilted portfolios for non-risk reasons (mandates, benchmarking, taxes, index membership), so the market price differs from the rational-agent value by a wedge that is a function of observable characteristics and mean-reverts as capital slowly moves.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: Define the traded price P~_it = P_it*W_it with log W_i,t+1 = theta*h(x_it) + u_i,t+1 and u_i,t+1 = rho_u*u_it + sigma_u*e_i,t+1, where x_it are date-t characteristics (so the wedge target is known at t) and e is independent of every payoff shock. The traded return is R~_i,t+1 = (P_i,t+1 W_i,t+1 + FCF_i,t+1)/(P_it W_it), and because W_i,t+1 factors into a t-measurable part times an independent lognormal, the conditional second moment is the existing ER multiplied elementwise by known constants - analytic, no new quadrature. The expected excess return acquires alpha_i = (1 - rho_u)*(theta*h(x_it) - u_it) plus a Jensen term: a premium with NO corresponding covariance loading. Choose h non-monotone and interactive, e.g. (rank size - 0.5 - c1)*(rank bm - 0.5 - c2) restricted to the top ivol tercile, or a sum of Gaussian bumps in (size, bm, ivol) space. Then alpha is orthogonal to the linear span of the characteristics by construction and alpha'D^{-1}alpha is O(N) - the near-arbitrage the theory requires. Combined with Proposal 1's dispersed d, the oracle experiment predicts a ceiling ratio of order 6-20x.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: By construction and verifiably: choose h to be exactly orthogonal, in each monthly cross-section, to {1, size, bm, agr, roe, mom, ...} and to the six FF factor weight vectors, by projecting the candidate h onto those columns and subtracting. Then the FM-attainable Sharpe from the alpha channel is exactly zero and FF's is exactly zero, while the RFF span contains h to whatever accuracy its effective rank permits. This is the one proposal where 'FM cannot capture it' is a theorem rather than an approximation argument. It is also the one where a referee will say the conclusion was assumed - which is why the orthogonalization should be applied to a plausible economic h (a bump in small-value-high-volatility space, where real anomaly returns actually concentrate) rather than to a random function, and why the paper must report the pricing of the rational component separately.
proposals.exact_change: (1) utils_bgn/panel_functions_bgn.py: after P is built (line 164) compute the date-t characteristics h needs from P, book and the existing arrays, form `logW = THETA_W*h(x) + u` with u an AR(1) drawn as a (T+1, N) array, set `Ptilde = P*np.exp(logW)`, and use Ptilde in the return at line 167 and in the panel's mve at line 212. (2) The eret block (lines 172-186) must be re-derived: 1 + eret~_i,t = exp(theta*h(x_it) + rho_u*u_it + 0.5*sigma_u^2)*(term1+term2+term3)/(P_it*W_it) + term4/(P_it*W_it) - the existing four terms rescaled by two known scalars per firm. (3) utils_bgn/sdf_compute_bgn.py: at line 285, where ER[1:,1:] is divided by np.outer(P[t+1], P[t+1]), the payoff legs carrying W_i,t+1 (the PRICE legs: terms 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8) must be multiplied by g_i = exp(theta*h_i + rho_u*u_it + 0.5*sigma_u^2) and, on the diagonal only, by the extra factor exp(sigma_u^2) since u_i,t+1 is perfectly correlated with itself; the cash-flow leg is NOT scaled. Cleanest implementation: build the length-N vector g, apply ER_price_legs *= np.outer(g, g) with the diagonal multiplied by exp(sigma_u^2), and divide by np.outer(Ptilde, Ptilde) at line 285. (4) config.py: THETA_W, RHO_U, SIGMA_U near line 206.
proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: Three parameters, all anchored on real-data quantities. (a) THETA_W and h's normalization set sd(alpha). The alpha channel's maximum squared Sharpe is alpha'D^{-1}alpha = N*E[alpha^2/d]. Real data: DKKM's complex SDF attains an annualized OOS Sharpe of ~3.7 versus the market's ~0.4, so the alpha channel supplies (3.7^2 - 0.4^2)/3.7^2 = 98.8% of the squared Sharpe, a monthly appraisal ratio of 3.7/sqrt(12) = 1.07. With N = 1000 and Proposal 1's idiosyncratic volatility of ~10.5%/month, sd(alpha) = 1.07*0.105/sqrt(1000) = 0.36%/month - 36 basis points per month of characteristic-driven non-risk expected return, squarely inside documented anomaly spreads. Set THETA_W*(1-RHO_U)*sd(h) = 0.0036 with h normalized to unit cross-sectional variance. (b) RHO_U governs how fast the wedge closes; anomaly half-lives in the limits-to-arbitrage literature are 1-3 years, so RHO_U = 0.97 monthly gives a 23-month half-life, hence 1 - RHO_U = 0.03 and THETA_W*sd(h) = 0.12, a 12% cross-sectional dispersion in the price wedge - comparable to documented valuation-error dispersion. (c) SIGMA_U is transitory demand noise; set it so the wedge contributes ~15% of idiosyncratic return variance, about 4%/month, which also keeps alpha only partially learnable (an important realism check: if alpha were perfectly learnable DKKM would attain a 3.7 Sharpe with no estimation loss).
proposals.predicted_effect: max_sr: rises sharply, from 0.26 to roughly 1.1/month if the calibration is hit - intentional, it is the real-data number, but the HJ bound must then be reinterpreted as a bound on the marginal investor's SDF rather than a representative agent's. FF/FM Sharpe: essentially unchanged in level (they still capture the rational component, ~0.25/month) and therefore collapse in RATIO terms to ~0.23 of max. DKKM: bounded by how much of h its basis represents; with Proposal 3's bandwidth and 3600 features expect 0.5-0.8 of max, i.e. 0.55-0.90/month. DKKM/FF 2.5-4x, the real-data target. HJD: as S* grows the true HJ portfolio return degenerates (E[sdf_ret] -> Rf, sd(sdf_ret) -> 0), so at S* ~ 1.1 the dynamic range between zero skill and perfect correlation is only ~25% of the level and every method's HJD converges toward 0.7-0.75. Switch to the scale-free HJD sqrt(1 - rho_uncentered^2) before running this, or the metric will hide the result it is meant to reveal.
risks: The obvious referee objection: the conclusion is assumed. The defense is that no frictionless model with a one-dimensional price of risk can produce the result - which the other five proposals demonstrate quantitatively - and that the wedge is calibrated to independently measured objects (anomaly half-life, anomaly spread magnitude), not chosen to win.

It changes what 'true' means. rp and cond_var now include the wedge, and the true HJ portfolio is the marginal investor's, not the representative agent's. State this explicitly or the HJD numbers are uninterpretable.

The wedge target must use only date-t information or ER stops being analytic. In particular h cannot depend on P_i,t+1, which rules out the most natural specification (a wedge on the contemporaneous valuation ratio) and introduces a one-month lag a referee may find arbitrary.

Because alpha is orthogonalized against the char columns each month, it is by construction invisible to FM; if the orthogonalization basis later changes, the result changes. Fix the basis once and document it.

At S* ~ 1.1/month both HJD and the mean-of-ratios Sharpe become fragile; the interpolating alpha = 0 DKKM column already produces near-hedged w_t with tiny denominators, and those months will dominate the average. Report the median and the pooled Sharpe alongside.
proposals.implementation_cost: Small to code, large in consequence. The second moment stays exactly analytic: log W_i,t+1 = theta*h(x_it) + u_i,t+1 splits into a t-measurable factor and an independent lognormal, so ER's price legs are multiplied by the deterministic outer product np.outer(g, g) with a scalar exp(sigma_u^2) correction on the diagonal - no new integral, no new interpolant, no change to the O(N^2) kron work. No solution file is re-solved: J*, optval and the beta calibration all live inside P_it, which the wedge multiplies from outside. The real cost is analytic care in re-deriving eret (lines 172-186) and in identifying which of terms 1-8 are price legs versus the cash-flow leg; get that wrong and cond_var is silently biased.

proposals.name: Heterogeneous project durability: two or three discrete survival types (requires re-solving Jstar)
proposals.one_line: Let projects be drawn from a small set of survival rates pi_m instead of the single PI = 0.99, so firms differ in asset duration and hence in interest-rate exposure independently of size and book-to-market.
proposals.economic_story: BGN is built on a Vasicek term structure and its dominant source of return variance is the revaluation of assets in place through D(r): the interest-rate loading A_xi has mean -0.039 against a cash-flow loading A_mu of +0.013, a 9:1 variance ratio. Yet every project has the same duration, because PI = 0.99 is a global constant entering D(r) = sum_k pi^k B(k, r) (vasicek.py lines 49-55). Consequently A_xi is 97.5% correlated with 1/mve and adds nothing beyond size. In reality assets differ enormously in duration - a retail lease and a pharmaceutical franchise decay at different rates - and duration is the classic determinant of interest-rate exposure. Giving projects M discrete durability types keeps BGN's identity intact (firms are still portfolios of heterogeneous projects; the heterogeneity is now two-dimensional, risk and duration, arguably closer to BGN's own narrative than the one-dimensional version) while making interest-rate exposure a second, independent cross-sectional dimension. Since the interest-rate factor is nearly unpriced in the current calibration (lambda_xi/lambda_mu = -0.178) it functions as an unpriced common factor with heterogeneous exposures that must be hedged; alternatively, raising |BETA_ZR| in the same re-solve makes it a genuine second priced factor.
proposals.mechanism_for_dkkm_gain: A firm's interest-rate loading becomes A_xi,i = sum over its live projects of exp(-beta_j)*D'_{m(j)}(r)/P_i, a durability-mix-weighted average. The mix is a point on the M-simplex and is not recoverable from (size, bm): two firms with the same market and book value can have completely different duration. What reveals the mix is history - payout yield (short-duration projects pay out relatively more per unit of value), the volatility and persistence of book value (short-duration projects die more often, so agr is more volatile), and the sensitivity of past returns to past rate changes. Recovering a simplex point from those signals is a classification problem: the map from (payout yield, agr volatility, past-return beta on rate changes) to mix weights is nonlinear, and the required hedge weight is the mix-weighted duration divided by the idiosyncratic variance. If BETA_ZR is also raised so the rate factor carries a real price, the firm's premium acquires a second, duration-driven component and the cross-section of expected returns stops being exactly two-dimensional - the same target as Proposal 2 reached by a more structural route.
proposals.why_ff_fm_cannot_capture_it: The hedge requires w_i proportional to (duration_i - duration_target)/d_i, where duration_i is a latent simplex-weighted average estimated from several noisy signals. FM applies a single linear coefficient to each signal; the efficient combination is a classifier whose output enters MULTIPLICATIVELY against 1/d, and neither the classification nor the multiplication is in the linear span. FF sorts size against one char at a time and cannot form the three-signal combination at all. I must flag a genuine weakness, however: FF's 2x3 double sorts DO contain a coarse size-by-payout interaction, so if the durability types happen to be nearly ordered by payout yield alone, a payout tercile sort recovers most of the mix and FF is not badly disadvantaged. To keep the argument airtight the types must be identified only by a COMBINATION of signals - e.g. two types with the same payout yield but different agr volatility - which requires deliberate choice of the pi_m and of the type-specific cash-flow parameters, not an arbitrary spread.

proposals.parameter_choice_and_derivation: Durability types: PI = 0.99 implies an expected project life of 100 months and essentially identical duration for every firm. Target the observed cross-sectional dispersion of equity duration - Dechow-Sloan-Soliman and the recent duration literature put implied equity duration between roughly 15 and 25 years across the value-growth spectrum, a spread of about 1.6x. Duration scales roughly as 1/(1 - pi*exp(-r)), so pi in {0.975, 0.99, 0.9965} gives expected lives of 40, 100 and 286 months and durations in the ratio 1 : 1.9 : 3.4 - deliberately wider at the project level so that firm-level mixes, which average ~6 projects, span roughly the 1.6x target. Equal type probabilities keep the average near the current calibration. BETA_ZR: currently corr_zr = BETA_ZR/(SIGMA_Z*SIGMA_R) = -0.00014/(0.4*0.002) = -0.175, so lambda_xi = SIGMA_Z*corr_zr = -0.070 against lambda_mu = 0.394, i.e. the rate factor carries 3% of the squared price of risk. Real term-structure premia are roughly a third of equity premia in Sharpe terms, so target lambda_xi/lambda_mu = -0.5 to -0.7: corr_zr = -0.55 gives BETA_ZR = -0.55*0.4*0.002 = -0.00044, lambda_xi = -0.22 and lambda_mu = 0.334, with |lambda| still 0.4 so the HJ bound is unchanged.
proposals.predicted_effect: max_sr: roughly unchanged with durability types alone (an unpriced factor with more dispersion lowers it slightly), modestly higher if BETA_ZR is also raised. FF/FM Sharpe: falls, because the linear span can hedge only one duration direction while the type mix is a two-simplex; expect FM from 0.95 of max down to 0.82-0.90. DKKM: 0.93-0.97 of max. DKKM/FM 1.05-1.18x - a MODEST proposal in isolation. HJD floors move from a 1.04x gap to perhaps 1.4x. I rank it last on impact per unit of work: it is the only proposal here that requires re-solving a solution file and multiplying the O(N^2) kron cost by M^2, and it buys less than Proposal 1, which is a single constant.
risks: Requires regenerating Jstar.csv once per durability type using the commented-out code at vasicek.py lines 123-174, which evaluates a triple nested sum (951 option maturities x 400 bond maturities x 100 Laguerre nodes) at every point of an adaptively refined r grid. Hours of compute per type, with no test of correctness beyond the internal refinement tolerance - and the kp14 experience with a stale G_func.csv solved under superseded parameters is the cautionary case.

sdf_loop cost multiplies by M^2 = 9 on terms 3, 5 and 7, and BGN's moments step already runs at n_jobs = 1 (config.py line 40, because forked workers get OOM-killed). This may make the moments step the binding constraint on the whole run. Consider M = 2.

If the durability types are nearly identified by payout yield alone, FF's size-by-payout double sort recovers most of the mix and the DKKM advantage largely evaporates. Choose type-specific parameters so no single characteristic orders the types.

Raising |BETA_ZR| changes D(r) and hence prob_in_money, so beta_star and scale must be re-fitted (vasicek.py lines 68-77) and the whole BGN calibration re-checked - E[num], mean bm and mean mve all move.

A_xi is already 97.5% correlated with 1/mve; if the duration mix ends up strongly correlated with firm size in equilibrium (larger firms holding older, longer-duration stocks), the new dimension collapses back into size and the proposal delivers nothing. Check corr(duration mix, log mve) in a pilot simulation before doing the Jstar re-solves.
proposals.implementation_cost: The largest of the six. The conditional second moment REMAINS analytic - every integral is still a Gauss-Hermite quadrature over r_{t+1}, just evaluated for each ordered pair of durability types - but the number of precomputed integrals grows from 3 to 3*M(M+1)/2 (data_integ_D_sq, data_integ_JD, data_integ_D_optval at sdf_compute_bgn.py lines 137-140) and terms 3, 5 and 7 must be summed over M^2 type pairs, so the dominant O(N^2 * nnz) kron work multiplies by 9 at M = 3 (by 4 at M = 2). Separately this is the only proposal that requires RE-SOLVING a shipped solution file: Jstar.csv must be regenerated once per type via vasicek.py lines 123-174, and again if BETA_ZR is changed, since BETA_ZR enters the sigma12 recursion and hence B(k, r) and D(r). Budget days, not hours, and add a regression test that the M = 1 special case reproduces the current moments exactly.
